chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Abdillah al-Mu'min, from Ibn Muskhan, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Beware of al-hukumah (judicial authority/governance), for al-hukumah is only for the Imam who is knowledgeable in adjudication, just among the Muslims, being a Prophet or the heir of a Prophet."
ai.seo_question: Who holds the exclusive right to judicial authority (hukumah) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates the exclusive nature of *al-hukumah* (judicial authority) as a divine prerogative reserved for the Prophet or his designated successor (*Wasi*), emphasizing that legitimate governance requires both deep jurisprudential knowledge (*ilm*) and moral justice (*adl*). This establishes the foundational Shia principle that political and judicial authority is not merely a social contract but a religious office contingent upon the leader's spiritual and intellectual qualifications, distinguishing the Imamate from general caliphates.
